fair_value.method: Horizon-date (Sep-2027) blend on a $6.00/lb realized copper / $4,000/oz gold deck: NTM EV/EBITDA 6.0x on ~$690M (35%), P/E 10x on ~$3.74 EPS (20%), SOTP with Furnas on a 60%-attributable basis risked at ~$0.40B (25%), 2027 FCF at a 9% yield (10%) and a long-term-deck NAV cross-check at ~$29 (10%); ~$150M horizon net debt, ~106M diluted shares. Blend = ~$35.9, rounded to $36.0.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) EBITDA ~$690M: ~84kt Cu (2027 outlook 75-85kt, 2028 80-90kt) = ~176M payable lb x ($6.00 realized - C1 $2.25) = ~$660M; Xavantina ~55koz mined gold (stockpile sales end mid-2027) at ~$2,200/oz cash margin = ~$120M; G&A/royalties/exploration ~-$100M; rounded to $690M. 6.0x (mid-tier copper range 5-7x, Brazil single-country discount offset by 2028 growth) = EV $4.14B less horizon net debt ~$0.15B = $3.99B / 106M sh.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Forward EPS ~$3.74: EBITDA $690M - D&A ~$165M (H1-26 run-rate ~$152M/yr plus Pilar shaft) - expensed interest ~$35M = $490M pre-tax x (1 - 19% tax; H1-26 effective ~17.5%) = ~$397M / 106M sh. Multiple 10x. The round-1 C$ consensus cross-check was dropped (mixed currencies).

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Caraiba+Tucuma+Xavantina at 5.0x NTM EBITDA $690M = $3.45B; Furnas: PEA after-tax NPV8 $2.0B is 100% basis at $4.60 Cu; Ero earns 60% (~$1.2B) and grants Vale up to an 11% construction free carry, so ~$1.1B attributable, risked at ~35% (PEA stage, PFS 2027, FID ~2029) = ~$0.40B; exploration incl. Odin ~$0.10B; less net debt $0.15B = $3.80B / 106M sh.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 FCF ~$327M: EBITDA ~$670M (80kt, H1 stockpile gold) - capex ~$230M (guided 'significantly lower' than 2026's $285-330M) - cash tax ~$75M - interest ~$38M = ~$3.08/sh at a 9% FCF yield.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Long-term-deck P/NAV cross-check: operating NAV at $4.75/lb LT Cu, $3,000 LT gold, 8% real, plus 2027-28 cash flows at the $6.00 deck, Furnas risked $0.40B, less net debt -> NAV ~$29-32/sh; at ~0.9-0.95x (mid-tier peers 0.82-0.95x on $4.00-4.50 LT decks, Skillings May-2026) = ~$29. Low weight because the Sept-2027 price is set mainly by near-term cash-flow multiples.

bear.story: Copper retraces to ~$5.0-5.4/lb realized (at or below Citi's ~$12,000/t base case) as tariff front-loading unwinds and LME stocks rebuild; the Pilar external shaft slips into 2028 or Tucuma throughput stalls, so 2027 guidance comes in at the low end of 75-85kt. NTM EBITDA ~$520M x 5x less ~$0.25B net debt -> ~$22.

base.story: Copper holds ~$5.75-6.30/lb realized (between Citi and Goldman's raised $13,800/t 2027 average); Ero delivers 2026 guidance and guides 2027 at 75-85kt with C1 ~$2.20-2.35 (BRL collars, floor 5.40, protect costs through Dec-2027); Pilar shaft operating in 2027; net debt ~$100-200M by Sep-2027 and capital returns start. Stock holds ~6x forward EBITDA.

bull.story: Structural deficit keeps copper at/above $6.75-7/lb, Pilar ramps on schedule toward 2028's 80-90kt, Furnas PFS comes in large and high grade, and Ero initiates a dividend/buyback from a near-net-cash balance sheet; NTM EBITDA ~$900M x 6.25x, ~net cash -> ~$53-58.

thesis_break_reason: At $23 the equity is ~$2.44B and EV ~$2.7B with ~$250M net debt, about 3.9x my ~$690M base-deck EBITDA and ~5.2x even at $5.00/lb copper (~$520M). Getting there needs copper sustained below ~$5/lb (under every current bank 2027 forecast: Citi ~$5.44, Goldman ~$6.26) or a company-specific failure: Pilar shaft slipping past 2027, Tucuma filtration not lifting throughput, 2027 guidance well below 75-85kt, or a Brazil fiscal/permitting shock. That is not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact checks, which I verified where they mattered, changed three things. (1) Furnas: the PEA's $2.0B NPV8 is on a 100% basis and Ero earns 60% while granting Vale up to an 11% construction free carry (confirmed in PEA coverage), so my risked value falls from $0.70B to ~$0.40B (-$2.8/sh on the SOTP). (2) Goldman raised its 2027 LME average to $13,800/t (~$6.26/lb) on 2026-06-01, so my bear anchor (old $10,750/t) was stale; I now anchor the bear on ~$5.0-5.4/lb (Citi base and below). (3) USD/BRL collars ($450M, floor 5.40, cap 6.34) run July 2026 to Dec 2027 (Q2-26 MD&A), so 2027 costs are partly hedged. I also accept a C1 of ~$2.25 (2026 guide $2.15-2.35, Q2 actual $2.42), recomputed EBITDA bottom-up from payable pounds (~$690M NTM vs $740M before), took D&A (~$152M/yr H1-26 run-rate, ~$165M with Pilar) and tax (~17.5% H1-26) from the MD&A, which puts forward EPS at ~$3.74 not $4.20, and dropped the mixed-currency consensus check. I added a low-weight (10%) long-term-deck NAV cross-check (~$29) because peers trade ~0.82-0.95x NAV on conservative decks; I disagree with a 20% weight since the horizon price is set mostly on near-term cash-flow multiples, and on my rough build NAV ranges widely. I kept horizon net debt at ~$150M (supervisor: $100-200M). Net result: fair value $38.6 -> $36.0, a little below the $37.87 price and below the supervisor's $37.5, mainly because my EBITDA build and EPS came in lower than round 1, not because I use a lower copper deck. Spot copper above my $6.00 deck gives some upward skew, so I centre the ladder median at ~$37 (P(>=38) 0.478, from 0.51), using a lognormal with ~48% sigma (below the 64% realized, which reflects a one-way rally, and well above large-cap base rates because of copper leverage and single-country, single-shaft risk), with the left tail fattened for a copper crash, Brazil or operational failure. Scenario mean (25% $22 / 50% $37 / 25% $56) is ~$38, consistent with a median of ~$37 and right skew. Thesis break moved from $25 to $23: at $25 the stock would still be ~5.5x EBITDA at $5 copper, which is ordinary copper-cycle risk rather than a broken thesis. Research this round: 3 web searches plus one MD&A fetch; no option data and nothing under priors/ was used.
